cues.en: So you came back from visiting Xerox PARC with a vision. Mhmm. And how did you implement the vision?
cues.zh: 所以你从参观 Xerox PARC 回来时，带着一个愿景。嗯。那你是怎么实现这个愿景的？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: I got our best people together and started to get them working on this.
cues.zh: 我把最优秀的人聚到一起，让他们开始着手做这件事。

cues.en: The problem was that we'd hired a bunch of people from Hewlett Packard,
cues.zh: 问题在于，我们招了一批来自 Hewlett Packard 的人，

cues.en: and they
cues.zh: 而他们

cues.en: didn't get this idea.
cues.zh: 没搞懂这个理念。

cues.en: They didn't get it. I remember having dramatic
cues.zh: 他们就是没搞懂。我记得和其中一些人有过激烈的

cues.en: arguments with some of these people who thought the coolest thing in user interface was soft keys at the bottom of a screen, you know. They had no concept of proportionally spaced fonts, no concept of a mouse. Matter of fact, I remember arguing with these folks, people screaming at me that it would take us five years to engineer a mouse and it would cost $300 to build.
cues.zh: 争论，他们觉得用户界面里最酷的东西是屏幕底部的软按键，你懂的。他们完全没有比例字体这个概念，也没有鼠标的概念。事实上，我记得和这些人争论，有人冲我嚷嚷说，我们要花五年时间才能把鼠标做出来，而且制造成本要 300 美元。

cues.en: And I finally got fed up. I just went outside and found David Kelley Design
cues.zh: 我最后实在受不了了，就直接出去找了 David Kelley Design

cues.en: and, asked them to design me a mouse, and in ninety days, we had a mouse we could build for $15
cues.zh: 请他们帮我设计一款鼠标。九十天后，我们就有了一款能以 15 美元的成本生产的鼠标

cues.en: that was phenomenally reliable.
cues.zh: 而且可靠性出奇地高。

cues.en: So I found that in a way, Apple
cues.zh: 所以我发现，从某种程度上说，Apple

cues.en: Apple did not have the caliber of people
cues.zh: Apple 当时没有足够优秀的人才

cues.en: that was necessary to seize this idea in many ways.
cues.zh: 来在很多方面抓住这个想法。

cues.en: And there was a core team that did, but there was a a larger team
cues.zh: 有一支核心团队做到了，但还有一支更大的团队

cues.en: that
cues.zh: 其中

cues.en: most had mostly had come from Hewlett Packard that that
cues.zh: 大多数人基本都来自惠普，他们

cues.en: didn't have a clue. Well, this this becomes this issue of professionalism. There's a dark side and a light side to it. Well, no. You know what it is? No. It's not dark and light. It's that people get confused.
cues.zh: 完全摸不着头脑。这就引出了职业精神这个问题。它有阴暗面，也有光明面。不，不对。你知道问题是什么吗？不，不是光明面和阴暗面，而是人们会搞混。

cues.en: Companies get confused. When they start getting bigger,
cues.zh: 公司会陷入迷茫。当规模开始变大时，

cues.en: they wanna replicate
cues.zh: 他们总想复制

cues.en: their initial success.
cues.zh: 最初的成功。

cues.en: And a lot of them think, well, somehow there's some magic in the process of how that success was created. So they start to try to institutionalize
cues.zh: 很多人会觉得，当初能成功，一定是流程里有什么秘诀。于是他们开始尝试在全公司

cues.en: process across the company.
cues.zh: 将流程制度化。

cues.en: And before very long,
cues.zh: 但没过多久，

cues.en: people get very confused that the process is the content.
cues.zh: 大家就把流程和实质内容给搞混了。

cues.en: That's ultimately the downfall of IBM. IBM has the best process people in the world. They just forgot about the content.
cues.zh: 这最终成了 IBM 衰落的原因。IBM 拥有全世界最懂流程的人，可他们却把实质内容给忘了。

cues.en: And that somewhat happened a little bit at Apple too. We had a lot of people who were great at management process.
cues.zh: 这种情况在 Apple 也有点类似。我们有很多人非常擅长管理流程。

cues.en: They just didn't have a clue as to the content.
cues.zh: 但他们对内容一窍不通。

cues.en: And in my career,
cues.zh: 在我的职业生涯中，

cues.en: I found that the best people,
cues.zh: 我发现最优秀的人，

cues.en: you know, are the ones that really understand the content, and they're a pain in the butt to manage.
cues.zh: 是那些真正懂内容的人，而他们管理起来特别让人头疼。

cues.en: You know? But you put up with it because they're so great at the content, and that's what makes great products. It's not process, it's content.
cues.zh: 你知道吗？但你得忍着，因为他们在内容上太出色了，而这才造就了伟大的产品。关键不是流程，而是内容。
